title: International schools in Ho Chi Minh City: fees 2026-2027
description: Nine international and bilingual schools in Ho Chi Minh City: IB, British or American, ward, ages, accreditation and 2026-2027 fees from each school's own page.
h1: International schools in Ho Chi Minh City: curriculum, area and 2026-2027 fees
intro: Most international schools in Ho Chi Minh City teach IB, British/Cambridge or American programmes, and most are in Thao Dien and Thu Thiem (old District 2), District 7 and the south. On 21 November 2026 eno.vn read the websites of nine schools, and on 22 November 2026 it read their fee pages again. Four of them publish their 2026-2027 fees as text on a web page. The others put them in a PDF, an image or a lookup tool.
keyPoints: According to each school's own 2026-2027 fee schedule, read on 22 November 2026, annual tuition at the four schools that publish figures on their web pages runs from {{vnd:196350000-1055300000}}, depending on the school, the year group and how you pay.
Tuition is not the whole bill. New pupils pay one-off fees too: SSIS charges a {{vnd:60000000}} registration fee, and ISHCMC's admissions fee is {{vnd:50000000}} for Grades 1-12.
Under Decree 86/2018/ND-CP, Vietnamese students on a foreign programme must be fewer than 50% of all students at a foreign-invested school.

Under Decree 360/2026/ND-CP, schools founded before 17 September 2026 must change their name by 17 September 2027 if the word "international" in it could mislead. A school's name does not tell you what kind of school it is.
eno.vn does not name a "best" school. Teachers' 2026 Teachers' Choice voting closes on 31 December 2026, and there are no results yet.

sections.title: Schools in Ho Chi Minh City: international and bilingual schools by curriculum

blocks.text: The international schools in Ho Chi Minh City follow three main curricula. **IB** is the International Baccalaureate (PYP, MYP and the Diploma). **British/Cambridge** leads to IGCSE and A Level. **American** schools teach to AP, and some add the IB Diploma. Some schools follow one system from nursery to Year 13 or Grade 12, and others change curriculum between stages. Everything in the table below comes from each school's own website, read on 21 November 2026. Where a cell says "not stated", the school's page does not say. It does not mean the school lacks it.

Since 1 July 2025 Ho Chi Minh City has had no official districts, so schools now give their addresses by the new ward or commune names. The table shows the ward each school publishes, with the old area name that parents and estate agents still use.

blocks.title: This list is not complete
blocks.text: Ho Chi Minh City has many more international and bilingual schools. This table includes only the schools whose curriculum and address eno.vn could read on the school's own website on 21 November 2026. To check that an accreditation is current, look the school up on the accrediting body's own site (CIS, WASC, NEASC, IB), or ask the school to show you the certificate.

sections.title: How much do international schools in Ho Chi Minh City cost in 2026-2027?

blocks.text: Of the four schools that publish 2026-2027 fees as text on a web page, the lowest annual tuition is {{vnd:196350000}}, for ABCIS half-day Pre-Nursery paid as one annual sum. The highest is {{vnd:1055300000}}, for Grades 11-12 at ISHCMC. All figures below come from each school's own fee page, read on 22 November 2026.

blocks.caption: Annual tuition for 2026-2027, from each school's own fee schedule (read 22 November 2026)
rows: Grade 1-12 tuition includes a {{vnd:67500000}} annual development fee. Admissions fee {{vnd:25000000}} (Early Explorers to Kindergarten) or {{vnd:50000000}} (Grades 1-12).

The instalment figures are SSIS's full fee. Paid in full by 25 June 2026, with a 6% discount, the same range is {{vnd:498380000-869073000}}, so SSIS's lowest fee is {{vnd:498380000}} paid upfront. Application fee {{vnd:10000000}}, registration fee {{vnd:60000000}}, enrolment deposit {{vnd:45000000}} (deducted from tuition).
Application fee {{vnd:5800000}}. Registration fee {{vnd:30000000-55000000}}, depending on grade.

The annual figures are for one payment by 1 August 2026; paying in 3 instalments costs more. Registration fee {{vnd:14500000-38400000}}. Refundable deposit {{vnd:22000000}} for Years 1-13 only (not payable for Pre-Nursery, Nursery or Reception), refunded on the pupil's last day, less anything owed, only if parents have given 90 days' written notice. BVIS's fee page sets the same 90-day written-notice rule for its deposit. IGCSE exams {{vnd:4800000}} a subject.

blocks.text: These schools publish a 2026-2027 fee schedule, but only as a PDF or an image, so eno.vn has not taken figures from them. Open the file on each school's own page: [BIS HCMC](https://www.nordangliaeducation.com/bis-hcmc/admissions/tuition-fees), [BVIS](https://www.nordangliaeducation.com/vi/bvis-hcmc/admissions/tuition-fees), [AIS](https://www.aisvietnam.com/admissions/fees) and [Canadian International School (CIS)](https://cis.edu.vn/vi/tuyen-sinh/hoc-phi). [VAS](https://www.vas.edu.vn/en/tuition-fees) has a 2026-2027 fee lookup tool where you choose a level, programme and campus, or you can register to be sent the fees. The EIS fees page gives no figures.

BVIS lists some one-off fees as text on its page: an application fee of {{vnd:3700000}}, an enrolment fee of {{vnd:73300000}} ({{vnd:24500000}} for Early Years) and a deposit of {{vnd:36700000}}. According to BVIS, its tuition includes lunch, required learning materials and international exam fees.

blocks.title: Compare the total cost, not tuition alone
blocks.text: Each school bundles its fees differently. ISHCMC's Grade 1-12 tuition already includes its development fee. SSIS charges separately for registration, lunch, the school bus and AP and IB exams, and requires pupils in Grades 4-12 to bring a MacBook every day. Before you compare schools, add up tuition, the one-off fees for a new pupil, the bus and lunch for the same year group.

sections.title: International kindergartens and elementary schools in Ho Chi Minh City

blocks.text: For 2026-2027, the cheapest annual early-years tuition eno.vn found is {{vnd:196350000}} (ABCIS, half day, paid annually). The most expensive is {{vnd:702400000}} (ISHCMC Kindergarten). Half-day and full-day places cost different amounts, so check the school day before you compare.

BIS HCMC publishes a separate PDF fee schedule for its Early Years Foundation Stage and Fundinotots, and BVIS takes babies from birth in Fundinotots (0-36 months).

sections.title: IB, A-level or American: which schools in HCMC teach what?

blocks.text: For A Levels in Ho Chi Minh City, ABCIS, BVIS and VAS's CAPI programme lead to A Level, according to their own websites. For the IB Diploma, look at ISHCMC, EIS, BIS HCMC, AIS and SSIS. For an American programme with AP, look at SSIS and TAS.

blocks.text: According to VAS's fee page, as of November 2026, Cambridge content makes up about 45-50% of its CEP programme, 50-65% of CAP and 70-85% of CAPI. Only CAPI leads to the A Level certificate.

sections.title: International school or bilingual school: what is the difference?

blocks.text: An international school teaches a foreign curriculum (IB, British or American), mostly in English, and leads to qualifications such as IGCSE, A Level or the IB Diploma. A bilingual school usually teaches the Vietnamese national curriculum with parts of an international one added, and the balance of English and Vietnamese varies from school to school. VAS's CEP programme combines the Ministry curriculum with Cambridge. BVIS follows the English National Curriculum and teaches pupils in both English and Vietnamese.

Bilingual schools can often give both Vietnamese and international qualifications, which suits families planning on a Vietnamese university. Families who may move country usually prefer a school that teaches one international curriculum from start to finish, because moving to another school is easier.
What the rules say and who licenses schools

items: **Foreign-invested schools** are governed by Decree 86/2018/ND-CP, in force since 1 August 2018. According to [LuatVietnam](https://luatvietnam.vn/tin-van-ban-moi/bo-quy-dinh-tre-duoi-5-tuoi-khong-duoc-hoc-truong-quoc-te-186-16738-article.html), it requires Vietnamese students on a foreign programme to be fewer than 50% of all students. It also dropped the old rule that kept Vietnamese children under 5 out of foreign programmes.

**Decree 124/2024/ND-CP** amended Decree 86. According to [VietnamPlus](https://www.vietnamplus.vn/giam-thu-tuc--siet-chat-luong-hop-tac-dau-tu-nuoc-ngoai-trong-giao-duc-post986419.vnp) (October 2024), a foreign curriculum taught in Vietnam must be recognised by a foreign education body or be quality-accredited, and must have been taught in its home country for at least 5 years. The school must also consult the local education authority on content and quality.

**Who licenses schools in Ho Chi Minh City**: according to [Báo Giáo dục Việt Nam](https://giaoduc.net.vn/tphcm-so-gddt-yeu-cau-truong-ten-goi-co-chua-cum-tu-quoc-te-quoc-gia-ra-soat-doi-ten-post263866.gd) (6 November 2026), the Director of the city's Department of Education and Training decides, within the powers delegated to the Department, on founding schools, licensing their teaching, suspending them and dissolving them.

**"International" in a school's name**: under Decree 360/2026/ND-CP, a school may not use "quốc tế" (international) or "quốc gia" (national) in its name if that could mislead about its legal status, its scope or state backing. According to [Luật sư Việt Nam](https://lsvn.vn/truong-co-ten-quoc-te-quoc-gia-gay-hieu-nham-phai-doi-ten-trong-12-thang-a179485.html), schools founded before 17 September 2026 that fall under this rule must complete a name change within 12 months, by 17 September 2027. The city's Department of Education asked schools to review their names in document 11687/SGDĐT-TCCB, signed on 30 October 2026.

blocks.title: Ask for the licence, not the name
blocks.text: A name such as "academy", "international" or "school centre" tells you nothing on its own. Ask the school to show you its founding decision and its licence to teach. These two documents show what kind of school it is, which curriculum it may teach and what qualification a graduate receives. If you still have doubts, the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Education and Training can tell you.

sections.title: Which is the best international school in Ho Chi Minh City?

blocks.text: There is no official ranking of international schools in Ho Chi Minh City, and eno.vn does not call any school the best. The right school depends on the curriculum your child needs, where you live and your budget. Three sources are more useful than a "best schools" list: independent accreditation and inspection reports, teachers who have worked at the school, and your own visit.

items: **Accreditation and inspection**: CIS, WASC, NEASC, the IB and BSO inspectors judge schools against published standards. For example, ABCIS links its 2024 BSO inspection report from its home page. Ask for the full report, not the quote on the home page.

**Teachers who worked there**: [eno.vn's school directory](/schools) lists international schools, bilingual schools and language centres in Ho Chi Minh City. Teachers who worked or interviewed at a school can vote for it and write a review, and a moderator reads every review before it appears. Most schools have few or no reviews so far.
**Teachers' Choice ranking**: teachers' voting for 2026 closes on 31 December 2026, and there are no results yet.
**Visit the school**: sit in on a lesson, and ask about class sizes, how many teachers leave each year and how new pupils get English-language (EAL) support.

blocks.text: If you are a teacher looking for work, see [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Schools near me: choosing by area and finding a home nearby

blocks.text: The international schools in Ho Chi Minh City are in three clusters. The east of Saigon covers Thao Dien, An Phu and Thu Thiem (old District 2). The others are Phu My Hung (old District 7) and Binh Hung and Nha Be in the south. The school run at rush hour can take a long time, so many families choose a school first and then rent nearby.

blocks.text: To find a home near a school, browse [homes for rent in Ho Chi Minh City on eno.vn](/c/rentals). The [HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) gives median asking rents by district and type of home for homes listed on eno.vn, and is updated regularly. [Rent prices in Ho Chi Minh City by district](/guides/rent-prices) has area-by-area figures, and [renting an apartment in Vietnam](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner) covers viewings and leases.

sections.title: How to choose a school and apply

items.title: Choose the curriculum
items.text: Decide where your child is likely to go to university and whether your family may move country. Then choose IB, British/Cambridge, American, or a bilingual model with Vietnamese qualifications.

items.title: Narrow by area and budget
items.text: Add tuition, one-off fees, the bus and lunch from each school's 2026-2027 fee schedule. Weigh that against the journey from home.

items.title: Check the licence and accreditation
items.text: Ask to see the school's teaching licence, and check its accreditation on the accrediting body's own site. Ask whether the school has to change its name under Decree 360/2026/ND-CP.

items.title: Visit and hear from teachers
items.text: Book a visit, read reviews in the [school directory](/schools) and ask how many teachers leave each year.

items.title: Apply and pay the place fees
items.text: Read the refund terms before you pay. For example, the fee pages of both BVIS and ABCIS say their deposit is refunded only if parents give the school written notice 90 days before the pupil's last day.

faqs.q: How much are international school fees in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: International school fees in Ho Chi Minh City for 2026-2027 vary a great deal between schools and year groups, from half-day nursery to the final years of secondary school. eno.vn checked the fee schedules that ISHCMC, SSIS, The American School and ABCIS publish on their own websites on 22 November 2026. The fees table on this page shows each school's lowest and highest annual tuition, and whether the figure is paid upfront or in instalments. New pupils also pay one-off application, registration or enrolment fees.

faqs.q: What is the best international school in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: There is no official ranking of international schools in Ho Chi Minh City, and eno.vn does not call any school the best. The right school depends on the curriculum a child needs (IB, British or American), where the family lives and the budget. Teachers' Teachers' Choice voting for 2026 closes on 31 December 2026, and there are no results yet. Compare accreditation, fees and a school visit before deciding.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an international school and a bilingual school?
faqs.a: An international school in Ho Chi Minh City teaches a foreign curriculum such as IB, British or American, mostly in English, and leads to qualifications such as IGCSE, A Level or the IB Diploma. A bilingual school usually teaches the Vietnamese national curriculum with parts of an international curriculum added, and may give both Vietnamese and international qualifications. The school's licence to teach shows which type it is.

faqs.q: Which schools in HCMC offer A levels?
faqs.a: According to their own websites, read on 21 November 2026, The ABC International School (ABCIS) and BVIS teach the British curriculum through IGCSE to A Level, and the CAPI programme at Vietnam Australia International School (VAS) leads to an A Level certificate. BIS HCMC teaches IGCSE and then the IB Diploma in its sixth form. Ask each school which A Level subjects it offers in the year your child would start.

faqs.q: Which IB schools are there in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: IB schools in Ho Chi Minh City include ISHCMC, which teaches the full IB continuum (PYP, MYP and DP), and EIS, which teaches IB to pupils aged 2 to 18, according to their own websites. BIS HCMC and AIS teach the IB Diploma after IGCSE, and SSIS offers the IB Diploma alongside AP. The American School teaches IB PYP and is a candidate school for the IB Diploma.

faqs.q: Can Vietnamese children attend international schools in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Vietnamese children can attend international schools in Ho Chi Minh City. Under Decree 86/2018/ND-CP, Vietnamese students on a foreign programme at a foreign-invested school must be fewer than 50% of all its students. The same decree dropped the old rule that kept Vietnamese children under 5 out of foreign programmes. Because of the cap, a school may have no places left for Vietnamese pupils in some year groups.

faqs.q: What age do international kindergartens in Ho Chi Minh City start?
faqs.a: International kindergartens in Ho Chi Minh City start at different ages, according to each school's own website. BVIS takes babies from birth in its Fundinotots class (0 to 36 months). The American School starts at 18 months, and AIS takes children from 1.5 years. BIS HCMC and EIS start at age 2, and ABCIS at age 3. Half-day and full-day places carry different fees.

faqs.q: Is a school with international in its name an international school?
faqs.a: The word international in a Ho Chi Minh City school's name does not prove that the school is foreign-invested or teaches a foreign curriculum. Decree 360/2026/ND-CP bars the word from school names where it could mislead about legal status, and schools founded before 17 September 2026 that fall under the rule must change their name by 17 September 2027. Ask to see the school's licence to teach.
